findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD.

A tray of raw ground beef is observed stored on a shelf over containers of cooked ground beef used for sandwiches in the reach in cooler across from the hand washing station. The PIC was shown and rearranged the items during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that foods are stored so that cross contamination of pathogens is not a concern.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle used for root beer on the fountain drink machine is observed heavily soiled on the inner surface during his inspection. The PIC was shown and cleaned the nozzle during this inspection to correct. He stated that they are soaked regularly. This helps but routine cleaning is still needed to maintain safe standards. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-303.11 Ice Used as Exterior Coolant, Prohibited as Ingredient. After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of FOOD such as melons or FISH, PACKAGED FOODS such as canned BEVERAGES, or cooling coils and tubes of EQUIPMENT, ice may not be used as FOOD. 

A gallon of tea is observed stored in the ice in the ice machine during this inspection. The PIC was shown and removed the item during this inspection to correct. Ensure that ice used for drinks is not used as a cooling or cold holding medium.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Allergen training is not available for the certified food protection manager (CFPM) during this inspection. This situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to renew prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD.

A tray of raw ground beef is observed stored on a shelf over containers of cooked ground beef used for sandwiches in the reach in cooler across from the hand washing station. The PIC was shown and rearranged the items during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that foods are stored so that cross contamination of pathogens is not a concern.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

Wet wiping cloths are observed on the counters throughout the kitchen. There is a CL smell to the cloths indicating that they are used for sanitizing. This was discussed with the PIC and they moved the cloths back to the bucket to correct. Ensure that all wiping cloths used in the kitchen are stored between uses in solution at all times.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Allergen training is not available for the certified food protection manager (CFPM) during this inspection. This situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to renew prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival the hand sink used for the kitchen was without paper towels. The PIC was notified and the towels were replaced during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Raw ground beef is observed over cooked beef and pickles in the refrigerator in the back. The PIC moved the items during the inspection to correct. Do not store raw meats over Ready-To-Eat foods in the coolers.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle of the root beer on the fountain drink machine is observed soiled. PIC indicated that they soak/clean the item weekly. This needs to take place more often. The item was cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that it is cleaned often enough to prevent accumulation of slime/mold.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Raw ground beef is observed over cooked beef and pickles in the refrigerator in the back. The PIC moved the items as the inspector was looking at them. Violation corrected immediately.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. 

The ice scoop is observed soiled on the handle and is in need of cleaning. The PIC was shown and the scoop washed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

A food employee was observed to not wash their hands prior to donning gloves and handling food. Education was conducted to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-303.11: After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of FOOD such as melons or FISH, PACKAGED FOODS such as canned BEVERAGES, or cooling coils and tubes of EQUIPMENT, ice may not be used as FOOD. 

A pitcher of tea is observed stored in the ice in the ice machine during this inspection. PIC removed the pitcher immediately to correct the violation. Ice used for drinks should be protected from contamination from any source prior to use.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Multiple moist rags are observed on counters throughout the kitchen. Wiping cloths should be stored between uses in their sanitizing solution. A discussion took place and the rags placed into the bucket or discarded to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the bucket of sanitizer for use in the kitchen did not register on the inspector’s test strips. PIC remade the solution to correct concentrations during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf).

A gallon of milk is observed in the refrigerator partially used and without a date marking. PIC indicated that the milk was opened Friday (2/10/23). This makes today day six of the seven for date marking. PIC placed a date marking on the milk during the inspection to correct the violation and they are instructed to ensure that date marking is maintained correctly for the TCS foods in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The baffles of the hood system are observed heavily soiled with dust. The situation was discussed with the PIC. They said that the system is cleaned yearly. Inspector stated that cleaning of the baffles needs to take place between the times where a professional company makes scheduled visits. PIC instructed to remove and clean the baffles as needed to maintain them clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

Ceiling above the storage coolers & freezers observed to be damaged. PIC stated this is caused by leaks that have been fixed throughout the facility, but the source of the leak above the coolers has not been fixed. He indicated that the leak in question should be repaired over the summer. Eliminate leak and repair ceiling so it is smooth & easily cleanable.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: Three wet wiping cloths observed on counters throughout the kitchen. Discussed with PIC, who stated that facility has switched to using a spray bottle of sanitizer. Cease use of wiping cloths with sanitizer spray bottle- use disposable paper towels with sanitizer spray bottle. Do not store damp cloths on the counter. They must be kept submerged in sanitizer solution.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Ceiling above the storage coolers & freezers observed to be damaged. PIC stated this is caused by leaks that have been fixed throughout the facility, but the source of the leak above the coolers has not been identified. Eliminate leak and repair ceiling so it is smooth & easily cleanable.
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Four-inch pan of ground beef observed covered, cooling on the counter. PIC stated that it began cooling at 10:45 or 11AM. At 1:30PM, the ground beef was 85F, probed. Discussed cooling practices and benchmarks. Foods must cool from 135F to 70F in two hours, and reach 41F in a total of six hours. CORRECTED- Food was voluntarily discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14 (A) Cooked TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70 F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 5ºC (41 F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Four-inch deep pan of ground beef observed covered with a lid and a towel, cooling on the counter. When cooling food, separate into small portions, use shallow pans, and cover loosely (or not at all if safe from contamination). CORRECTED— Ground beef had not reached 70F within 2 hours of cooling, and was voluntarily discarded.
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans; Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Pitcher of iced tea observed stored in the ice machine containing ice intended for use in beverages. CORRECTED— Iced tea removed. Ice intended for consumption cannot be used for cooling.
3-303.11: After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of FOOD such as melons or FISH, PACKAGED FOODS such as canned BEVERAGES, or cooling coils and tubes of EQUIPMENT, ice may not be used as FOOD. [P]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Two wet wiping cloths observed on counters throughout the kitchen. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC, who returned cloths to newly prepared sanitizer bucket. Do not store damp cloths on the counter. They must be kept submerged in sanitizer solution.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. [C]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Single-service forks and spoons observed stored in one bin, with forks going one direction and spoons going the other. Picking up a spoon would result on contamination of the eating end of a fork. CORRECTED— Provided education and discussed with PIC. Utensils rearranged to prevent potential contamination of food-contact portions.
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. [C]

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Observed ice scooped using a cup with no handle. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC. Use a scoop with a handle to scoop. This prevents contamination of the ice from hands. Ice scoop is available. Proper use of ice scoop observed after discussion.
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under ¶¶ 3-301.11(B) and (E). [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed sandwiches prepared by placing the buns directly on the countertop that had not been sanitized or protected in any way from contamination. For example, inspector's clipboard had been set on that section of countertop just before sandwiches were prepared there. CORRECTED-- Provided education and discussed with PIC. Sanitize surfaces before using for food prep or use a barrier such as paper sandwiches will be wrapped in.
3-304.11: FOOD shall only contact surfaces of (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Six spray bottles observed either unlabeled, or labeled with "sanitizer." Contents of the bottles ranged in color (blue, purple, clear, and yellowish). CORRECTED-- PIC labelled spray bottles with their contents. Any bottles with unknown contents were discarded.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Three wet wiping cloths observed on counters throughout the kitchen. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC, who returned cloths to newly prepared sanitizer bucket. Do not store damp cloths on the counter. They must be kept submerged in sanitizer solution.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket that was presented upon arrival observed to be sudsy. PIC stated that it contained both Cl sanitizer and soap. Do not mix soap and sanitizer. CORRECTED-- Provided education. PIC prepared a bucket of Cl sanitizer ONLY (mixed with water) at a concentration of 100ppm. Sanitizer must be prepared during all times of food prep and service.
4-303.11: (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment: Bowl of ground beef observed cooling on the counter. PIC stated that it began cooling at 1PM. At 3PM, the ground beef was 100F, probed. Discussed cooling practices and benchmarks. Foods must cool from 135F to 70F in two hours, and reach 41F in a total of six hours. CORRECTED- Food was moved to shallow pans and placed in the freezer to rapidly cool.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14 (A) Cooked TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70 F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 5ºC (41 F) or less. (P)

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Bowl of ground beef (mentioned in Violation 20) observed cooling on the counter, covered by deli paper without any cooling methods being used to bring food to 70F in 2 hours, or to 41F or below in 6 hours. CORRECTED- Discussed cooling methods with PIC. Food was moved in shallow pans and placed in the freezer to rapidly cool.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15 Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: REPEAT: Observed wooden utensil used to put mustard on buns. Wood is not permitted for food-contact use. Replace utensil with something other than wood. PIC removed the wooden utensil from use.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.17 (A) Except as specified in ¶¶ (B), (C), and (D) of this section, wood and wood wicker may not be used as a FOOD-CONTACT SURFACE. (C)

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed handwashing sink with no paper towels provided (empty dispenser). CORRECTED- PIC refilled dispenser with paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with (A) Individual, disposable towels. (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed sanitizing sink of 3 compartment sink to have Cl concentration of 10ppm. CORRECTED- PIC remade sanitizing compartment to correct concentration.
4-501.114 (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the 2017 FDA Food Code. (P)

Observed 3 compartment sink set up as: wash, sanitize, rinse. PIC stated that it is used in the correct order, but is easier to use set up in this configuration. CORRECTED- Discussed correct order with PIC and provided education.

Observed cups being used as ice scoop at the shake station. Provide ice scoop with a handle to prevent bare hand contact with ice. Inspector will follow up in 10 days.
Reference 3-304.11 (A) FOOD shall only contact surfaces of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified
under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code. (P)

Observed brown build up in the ice machine. Inspector will follow up in 10 days.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed blue wet wiping cloths stored throughout the kitchen on counters. All wet wiping cloths must be stored submerged in sanitizer solution.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14 (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. (C)

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed wooden utensil used to put mustard on buns. Wood is not permitted for food-contact use. Replace utensil with something other than wood.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.17 (A) Except as specified in ¶¶ (B), (C), and (D) of this section, wood and wood wicker may not be used as a FOOD-CONTACT SURFACE. (C)

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed staff to go between food prep and other activities without washing hands or changing gloves. Hands should be washed after any activities that may contaminate hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 (I) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed kitchen handsink without paper towels available. Corrected by providing paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 (A) Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with individual, disposable towels.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  Ketchup stored next to raw hamburger. Store raw meats away from ready-to-eat foods to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed soda nozzle to be soiled. PIC then washed nozzle without sanitizing. Provided education and nozzles will be properly cleaned and sanitized.
4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed milkshake cups being stored on towels. Observed condiments to be stored in cardboard boxes. All non-food contact surfaces should be designed to be easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-202.16 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed a box being used to store ketchup and mustard bottles in the cold holding unit. Observed towels to be on the counterunder milk shake cups. 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. Use smooth cleanable items for storage in the facility. Replace cloth with cleanable plastic or rubberized material. Replace cardboard with cleanable material - meatl or plastic.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Area around fry station is soiled with grease and salt. Clean and maintain free of soil. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed box of single use cups on the floor in the back storage area. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.
Observed the employee to touch single use fork tines when placing the forks into the storage container.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.
750-880 Single-service knives, forks and spoons packaged in bulk shall be inserted into holders to protect these items from contamination and present the handle of the utensils to the consumer unless the utensils are pre-wrapped or pre-packaged. Take care when handling single service items.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed a hookah within the food areas, by the coolers in the rear. Ensure that tobacco equipment and products are stored outside of food areas. Hookah was moved during the inspection. 
750-530c Employees may use tobacco in any form only in designated areas. Areas shall not be designated for that purpose if the use of tobacco might result in the contamination of food, equipment, utensils or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink to be out of paper towels. Paper towels provided during the inspection. 
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed the fry hot holding area to have an accumulation of food debris and to be soiled in nature. After discussing this area with the owner, the owner states they clean this particular equipment once a week. This is inappropriate as food debris from several days of accumulation, and not being properly temperature, are allowed to contact fresh food. Ensure that this food contact surface is cleaned regularly to prevent a potential for cross contamination. Owner cleaned the fry station during the inspection. 
750-160(a) Food shall be prepared with the least possible manual contact, using suitable utensils and using surfaces that have been cleaned, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the soda spouts to have an excessive accumulation of dried debris. Ensure that the soda spouts are regularly cleaned to prevent a potential for cross contamination. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed a bottle of red chemicals in the bathroom that was unlabeled. Upon testing the bottle, it was found to be quat sanitizer. Ensure that all chemical bottles are properly labeled to prevent a potential for misuse/cross contamination. Bottle was labeled during the inspection. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed a scoop being stored in the relish without a handle extending out. Ensure that food dispensing utensils are stored in one of the manners listed below to avoid potentials for cross contamination. 
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the soda diffuser to have an accumulation of debris. Ensure that these surfaces are washed, rinsed, and sanitized at an interval that keeps them consistently clean from debris. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed the catch tray beneath the fry bin to be soiled with an accumulation of fry crumbs. The fry bin should be emptied nightly and removed for cleaning. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the hood ventilation to have an excessive accumulation of dust. Label on side of vent states the last cleaning was in 2013. The owner states it is done every 6 months, but referenced the ANSUL inspection tag. It was explained to the owner that these two are separate and that the hood should be cleaned regularly by a professional. 
750-1210e  Equipment attached to walls and ceilings shall be easily cleanable and shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed a container of dill pickles that contained a yellow substance. The yellow substance was identified to be mustard. Ensure that if the the bulk item is removed from its original container that it is relabeled with the proper label. 
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed the facility to be cooling ground beef on top of a soda syrup rack in a bowl. The initial temperature taken was 118F probed. The owner took the bowl and placed it into two separate containers for cooling, then placed them in the freezer. The beef started the cooling process at 11:45 per the owner. Temperature was rechecked at 13:45 with temperature findings of 78F in one container and 94F in the other. Owner stated he would take the product home as personal food. Ensure that PHFs go through the proper cooling process. They should be cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and 70F to 41F in 4 hours. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment:
1) Observed the owner preparing RTE food with bare hand contact. When preparing RTE foods gloves should be utilized to decrease the chances of cross contamination. 
750-160(a) Food shall be prepared with the least possible manual contact, using suitable utensils and using surfaces that have been cleaned, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent cross-contamination.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
1) Observed a container of relish being stored in the cooler. This container had a lid, with the non-food contact surface touching the relish, and a rag stored above this lid, then another container stored inside this container. Ensure that all proper measures are taken to prevent the potential for cross-contamination. Do not store rags in between containers or the non-food contact surface on top of food. Rag was moved during the inspection. 2) Weed eater was being stored in an area that was above clean rags intended to be used as sanitizer rags. Ensure that the items to be used for sanitization within the facility are not at risk of being contaminated. Weed eater was moved during the inspection. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment:
Observed multiple occurrences where a dish item skipped a step in the wash, rinse, and sanitize process. These occurrences were identified and brought to the owners attention for proper washing, rinsing, and sanitizing. Ensure that dirty dishes go through all 3 processes to reduce the chance of cross contamination. 
750-820a For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the three compartment sink to have a leak from the faucet. Ensure that the faucet is repaired or replaced so that it is in a good working order. 
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ceiling in the rear of the facility to have a hole and mesh exposed. Ensure that the ceiling is repaired so that it is smooth and easily cleanable. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed a canister of ant & roach killer being stored alongside the soda syrups and soda syrup rack. There are also other chemicals stored throughout the food prep areas that should be contained to one area that is below and away from food. Chemicals were moved during the inspection. 
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed multiple spray bottles labeled "cleaner". These bottles contained multiple different chemicals that varied in colors. One of them was tested to be a quat sanitizer. There were two bottles where the chemicals were unidentifiable. These bottles were discarded during the inspection. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed milk in a back cooler to be open. Manager states that the milk was bought and opened on Friday. Ensure that PHFs are dated with the date that they were opened and not used past 7 days. Manager was allowed to date mark the milk.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed ground beef that had already been cooked and placed in a cooler for cooling. Manager states he cooked the beef at 1100 and started the cooling process at 1200. Temperature was taken at 13:45 showing a temperature of 92F. The manager was allowed to place the container into the freezer to attempt to cool to 70F. The beef was at 87F after the time reached 14:00. The manager was instructed to reheat the product, but the manager did not want to reheat it. He stated it would take too long to reheat it due to the fact that they use a steam cooker. Manager stated he wanted to give it to his employees as personal food at this point. Manager was allowed to do so. Ensure that PHFs that are cooked are cooled to 70F within 2 hours and 41F or below within the 4 hours after that. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed active food prep occurring, as well as dish washing occurring, during the inspection. Both sanitizer buckets and the three compartment sanitizer sink were tested for Cl showing approx. 10 ppm. Manager was instructed that the sanitizer concentration needed to be at least 50 ppm for proper sanitizing. 
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a cloth that was wet underneath one of the ice machine lines. The cloth was folded and appeared to be placed at a junction in the PVC piping coming from the ice machine. The manager stated that he was unaware of any leaks. Manager stated he would further look into a possible leak. Moist cloths should be stored in a sanitizer solution or a designated dirty laundry area if they are no longer going to be used. Manager moved the cloth at this time.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the soda fountain to have an accumulation of debris inside the nozzles. Ensure that the nozzles are washed, rinsed, and sanitized regularly. Also, ensure that where the nozzles attach are cleaned regularly. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment:
Observed cleaned and stored single service containers in the back on top of a refridgerator. The manager states they save them in case any customers require one for personal use. Further in the inspection it was noted the facility was making sun brewed tea within the single service containers. The manager was advised that this was not allowed and that single service articles should be discarded following use and not reused. 
750-600 Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
Observed dirty mop water, appeared murky and without bubbles, being stored in the back near the chest freezer. Employee stated the water was from this morning. Mop water is considered waste water. Ensure that it is emptied after every use. 
750-1050 All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed a gap forming in between the coving and the wall behind the ice machine. There is also a gap formed allowing the corners of the coving to be displaced. Caulking this area was discussed with the manager during the inspection and he stated he was working on repairs. Ensure that floors are maintained in good repair, including the coving, as well as in a clean state.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ceiling in the back area by the three freezer and one cooler to be starting to be flaking, mesh was exposed, and the ceiling was bowing. The manager was notified and he stated that the repairmen were looking for the source of the leak before repairing the ceiling. They were required to wait for another rain to check for a source of the leak. Ensure that ceilings, walls, and attached fixtures are maintained in good repair, as well as in a clean state. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed a mop being stored in the mop bucket in between uses. The mop should be stored inverted or hanging to allow it to drip dry. Mop was removed from bucket and placed into use during the rest of the inspection. 
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak at the three compartment sink. Repair the leak.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Facility does not currently have an FSSMC. The owner is in the process of renewing his certificate. A spot check will be conducted in 90 days.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.
Observed that the hand sink towel dispenser was empty when the inspector arrived. A supply of sanitary towels (single-use, disposable) should be available for employees to properly wash hands before food preparation.
Corrected=the roll of towels was replaced in the unit.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the cooling vent louvers of the drink dispensing machine have some accumulation of dust. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Clean the vent louvers.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed that there are 2 floor tiles in front of the ice machine that are cracked.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors. Repair floor tiles.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750.1200a-Floors shall be smooth,durable, and maintained in good repair.
Repair floor tiles that are in disrepair.
Observed floor tiles in front of the 3 compartment sink, and infront of the ice machine that are cracked, chipped, or missing.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
750.120a-Food shall be protected at all times from potential contamination.
Store food products away from toxic chemicals to avoid potential for cross-contamination.
Observed containers of syrup stored on the same shelf next to latex paint cans.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed that the water flow from the faucet in the men's restroom is inadequate for hand washing. 
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.
CORRECTED= a new aerator was placed onto the spigot, and flow was restored.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the coving along the drive-through wall is missing.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.
Replace coving in this area.
Repeat violation. = Mr. Quasi has been waiting to complete this repair until the new floor tiles are installed.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the peeling and chipped paint in the ceiling of the store room.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.
Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
Repeat violation. = Mr. Quasi will complete this repair when warmer spring weather is here, temperatures below 0* has hampered his completing these repairs. The new roof has been installed last fall, but interior repairs were not completed prior to winter.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed a flourescent light fixture in the store room that was missing the light shield.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.
Provide properly shielded lights.
